top_choice_rationale: Targeted protein degradation is a mechanism that was designed and then measured: a bifunctional molecule forms a ternary complex whose cooperativity and linker dependence are quantifiable, and Ciulli's VHL-ligand and ternary-complex structures explain why degraders work. The principle is reproduced across many laboratories and gives acute, selective protein removal. Crews and Deshaies hold priority for the concept and Ciulli the structure-guided step, so a citation limited to PROTACs and the ubiquitin-proteasome system is defensible with three names. P003 (Handa as third) ranks next because it keeps the same field but shifts the citation toward the glue lineage, merging two origins; Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling (P002) is mature and well attributed but extends the 2010 cross-coupling logic; no award is last because a sound candidate exists.
